newsitem.title: USA: Everest Medical sees improved margins.
newsitem.headline: Everest Medical sees improved margins.

text.p: Everest Medical Corp, which reported a wider 1997 first quarter loss, said Monday it expects improved margins for the balance of the year.

"Our first-quarter gross margin is not representative of what we expect for the full year," said John Shannon Jr, president and chief executive officer, in a statement. "We expect to benefit from improvements in production efficiencies in subsequent quarters."
Everest on Monday reported a 1997 first quarter loss of $310,139 or $0.06 a share, compared with a loss of $124,008 or $0.04 in the same period last year.
Everest said its gross margin was reduced by early product-cycle costs as the company ramped up production of new instruments to meet strong demand.
Revenues rose 16 percent over the same period last year to $1.5 million reflecting a 43-percent increase in the sales of Everest-branded laparoscopy instruments.

Operating expenses increased during the first quarter from efforts to fulfill ISO 9000 and CE Mark certification and from development and marketing activities aimed at Everest's participation in the minimally invasive cardiovascular surgery market.

Shannon said the company is moving forward with its effort to export Everest's electrosurgical technology to the minimally invasive cardiac surgery market. The company has added a cardiovascular product manager, he said.
Everest designs, makes and markets bipolar electrosurgery instrumentation for the minimally invasive surgery markets.
Shares of Everest were trading at 1-7/8, off 1/4 from the close on April 18.
